title: Torsional Coupling
model_title: Highly Flexible Torsional Coupling (Rubber Element) — Engine Flywheel to Driven Shaft

introduction.definition: A highly flexible torsional coupling links an engine flywheel to a driven machine through a soft rubber element. Its low torsional stiffness shifts the shaft system's natural frequencies away from the engine's firing orders, and rubber hysteresis damps torque pulsations, protecting gears and generators.
applications: Diesel generator sets and marine propulsion

pressure.title: Soft in torsion: detunes and damps vibration
pressure.description: A reciprocating engine delivers torque in pulses (here 6 per revolution). The soft rubber element lets the flywheel and the driven hub twist relative to each other, so the large flywheel oscillation (yellow mark) is strongly reduced at the hub. Choosing the torsional stiffness moves the system's torsional natural frequencies away from the engine firing orders (a torsional vibration analysis, TVA), and rubber hysteresis damps what remains; the damping heat must stay within the element's allowable power loss.

video_tutorials.title: Torsional Coupling — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Torsional Coupling.
A highly flexible torsional coupling links an engine flywheel to a driven machine through a soft rubber element.
Its low torsional stiffness shifts the shaft system's natural frequencies away from the engine's firing orders, and rubber hysteresis damps torque pulsations, protecting gears and generators.
Typical applications include diesel generator sets and marine propulsion; engine-driven pumps and compressors.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Engine Flywheel, Ring Gear & Outer Flange (driving side), Inner Hub & Driven Shaft (generator / pump / gearbox).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Torsional Coupling.
Look for rubber dust or cracks.
Measure twist marks / check bolts.
Replace elements per hours / ageing.
Watch for element overheating: cracks, burning smell. Common cause: running near resonance, misfire.
Watch for bolt loosening: knocking. Common cause: wrong torque.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
